newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Competition concerns may hurt Man Yue market debut.
newsitem.headline: Competition concerns may hurt Man Yue market debut.

text.p: Concerns about fierce competition in the electronics industry may hurt the market debut of Man Yue International Holdings when its shares begin trading in Hong Kong on Wednesday, analysts said.
"We see keen competition in the industry and that can affect earnings in the longer term," said Kinson Au, senior analyst at PW Asia Brokerage.
Man Yue makes and sells capacitors and resistors which are mostly used in consumer electronic products.
Analysts said its earnings growth should be stable but unexciting.
"The industry is quite mature and demand for the products is expected to be very stable," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.
"There is nothing exciting in the business."
Man Yue issued 55 million new shares at HK$1.08 each in an initial public offering in Hong Kong which was 10.2 times subscribed.
"Investors are likely to switch to other new listings. When there are many choices in the market, why put a bet on one which appears unexciting?" one analyst said.
Man Yue said net proceeds of the issue would be used to raise its stake in a factory in Shenzhen, China, to install, expand and upgrade machinery and production capacity and to repay debt.
